label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: share one brief, one board and one hold
findings.why: Board and hold are used in the five steps before anything has said what they are, and the formula is the page I would act on.

findings.quote: I make the moving pictures in my workshop.
findings.why: Nine one-line hellos use names (ruv-sgit, Studio, Motion) that mean nothing yet, so I skim the list instead of learning who is in the team.

findings.quote: security's, planned in the first hour and never filled on the day
findings.why: It hints at a gap in the team, which interests me, but gives no reason and no pointer to where it is explained.

findings.quote: Read it the whole way through, or take the short way
findings.why: It tells me how to read the book, which a busy reader may take as being managed.

findings.quote: The VoiceDebrief pitch added the presenter
findings.why: Three earlier projects are named with dates and no explanation, which a reader with a conference to prepare will skip.

findings.quote: There is one more thing I want you to see as you read.
findings.why: It directs what I should look at, and the paragraph after it is a list of roles that I cannot yet place.

findings.quote: this one has a cast, scenes, a clock in the margin and pictures that do the explaining
findings.why: A triad that sells the book's style instead of telling me what a team like mine would take from it.

findings.quote: Then tell me what you think.
findings.why: The page ends on an invitation with no channel (the note says it is a gap), and with no takeaway on this page I would not read on from it.

findings.quote: At the other's next slot on the clock
findings.why: The slot is the idea that makes the mail work, and it is used here before I am told that each agent wakes at set times.

findings.quote: The talk's team kept its mail and its board in two public vaults
findings.why: Vaults appear without explanation and next to this book's own repository, and I cannot tell which setup I should copy.

findings.quote: a letter is a file, an answer is a file
findings.why: The same line is said again at 64 (a letter is a file in a folder) and again in the closing card.

findings.quote: Asked at my slot. Answered at the researcher's. Used at my next. I never had to ask twice.
findings.why: A run of four short sentences that restates what the three notes just showed.

findings.quote: No "just checking in". No "any update?". No message sent because somebody was anxious.
findings.why: Three short fragments in a row, and the reason for them is given in the next sentence anyway.

findings.quote: carry no Agent trailer, so agents.py check counts none of them
findings.why: Jargon from the talk team's tooling in a quoted note, with no gloss, so the example about a housekeeping request loses me.

findings.quote: the third of the three letters above, with its order of work, E09 first and E04 after
findings.why: The third letter and its order of work were told in full at line 60 and again in the ruv-sgit line that follows.

what_holds: 00-start-here.md: five steps on one page, short enough to try tomorrow with the agent I already have, and the line 'If you only read one page, read this one' respects my five minutes.
00b-who-is-telling-this-story.md: the narrator saying plainly that he speaks from now, with hindsight, and that the agents' scenes are dramatised.
10-talking-through-git.md: files as the way agents talk is a pattern I could copy this week, the three-letter example is concrete, and the closing 'Something to try' gives me a first step.
notes: Deal-breaker check: 'a story with no takeaway' is nearly tripped by 00b, which is about the book itself; the other two sections pass. 'One central person' is not tripped, since nothing in 10 needs the editor awake. As an event team I miss, in these three sections, how the factory stops (only a hint, 'the hold') and who owns the brief when several people share it.
